title: Nonthermal fixed point for massless scalar field theories
authors: Viktoria Noel, Chuang Huang, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Jürgen Berges
abstract: We compute universal scaling exponents and scaling functions for massless scalar field theories far from equilibrium. Using a large-$N$ expansion to next-to-leading order, we investigate the nonperturbative infrared behaviour associated with the transport of a) energy or b) effective particle number towards low frequencies $ω$ and momenta $\bar p$. For massless dispersion $ω= \bar{p}$, we determine the scaling form of the distribution function whose universal power-law tail $f_S(\bar p) \sim 1/\bar{p}^κ$ is found to be a) $κ= d+1$ and b) $κ= d$ in $d=3$ spatial dimensions. Our results establish that relativistic and nonrelativistic theories do not belong to the same universality class in this case, which opens up new applications to far-from-equilibrium phenomena in high-energy and (quantum) many-body physics with linear dispersions.
summary: This work calculates the universal scaling exponents for massless scalar field theories far from equilibrium by analyzing the non-perturbative infrared behavior. Using a large-N expansion, the authors find distinct scaling laws for energy versus particle number transport. The results highlight that relativistic and nonrelativistic theories belong to different universality classes in this non-equilibrium regime.
main_problem: The paper investigates the universal scaling exponents and scaling functions for massless scalar field theories when driven far from equilibrium.
main_result: It determines that the universal power-law tail exponent $\kappa$ for the distribution function is $d+1$ for energy transport and $d$ for effective particle number transport in $d=3$ dimensions.
method: The analysis employs a large-$N$ expansion to next-to-leading order within the 2PI effective action framework, analyzing self-similar scaling solutions.
model_or_system: The model is a relativistic scalar field theory with $O(N)$ symmetry, analyzed in $d$ spatial dimensions, considering the transport of energy or effective particle number.
key_observables: The universal power-law tail $f_S( ar p) \sim 1/ ar{p}^\kappa$ of the nonthermal scaling distribution function, and the scaling exponents $\kappa$.
important_parameters: Spatial dimension $d$, the nature of transport (energy vs. particle number), and the massless dispersion relation ($\omega =  ar{p}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes spatially homogeneous and isotropic systems, and relies on the existence of self-similar scaling solutions in the classical-statistical limit.
figures_summary: Figure 1 diagrammatically shows the retarded propagator $G_R$ and statistical function $F$, along with the diagrammatic expression for the self-energy $\Sigma_R$.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by setting up the field theory, deriving equations of motion for correlation functions, applying scaling assumptions to find fixed-point equations, and finally solving for the universal exponents based on conservation laws.
why_interesting: The findings on non-equilibrium scaling exponents and the distinction between relativistic and nonrelativistic universality classes are highly relevant for understanding far-from-equilibrium dynamics in quantum many-body systems, including those modeled by quantum gases.
